questions.q: Define verbal irony and situational irony in your own words, giving one example from daily life for each.
questions.a: Verbal irony: saying the opposite of what is meant (e.g., "Great job!" when someone drops a plate). Situational irony: outcome contradicts expectations (e.g., a fire station burns down). A wrong answer that confuses the two — e.g., calling a sarcastic remark "situational irony" — reveals the student cannot distinguish between language-based and circumstance-based irony, a distinction essential for analyzing Muktibodh's self-mocking tone versus the poem's structural contradictions.

questions.q: In "vkReifjp;", the speaker declares: "I am the enemy of darkness" (eSa Lusg&lqjk dk iku fd;k djrk gw¡). Explain why this statement functions as verbal irony in the context of the whole poem.
questions.a: The claim is verbal irony because the poem subsequently reveals the speaker's complicity with darkness — his compromises, fears, and failure to act — making him an unwitting ally of the very darkness he denounces. A student who treats this as a straightforward heroic declaration misses Muktibodh's central technique: the speaker's self-portrait is an indictment, not a celebration. This error shows inability to read against the grain of the speaker's own assertions.

questions.q: Identify ONE symbol in "xhr" (the poem beginning "fnu tYnh&tYnh <yrk gS!") and explain what abstract idea it represents, citing the specific lines where it appears.
questions.a: The "long, tedious day" (tYnh&tYnh fnu) symbolizes the oppressive stagnation of colonial/post-colonial existence where time drags without meaningful progress. It appears in the refrain "fnu tYnh&tYnh <yrk gS!" and the description of children growing up in darkness. A wrong answer that treats the day merely as literal weather description misses the symbolic compression of historical inertia into a sensory experience — a hallmark of Muktibodh's symbolism.

questions.q: Compare the function of the "lamp" (ljk) in "vkReifjp;" with the "night" (nqfu;k) in the same poem. How do these two symbols interact to structure the poem's central conflict?
questions.a: The lamp symbolizes fragile, individual consciousness attempting illumination ("eSa Lusg&lqjk dk iku fd;k djrk gw¡"), while night represents the overwhelming socio-historical darkness of ignorance, oppression, and false consciousness ("nqfu;k vius O;aX;&ck.k vkSj 'kklu&iz'kklu ls pkgs ftruk d"V ns] ij nqfu;k ls dVdj euq"; jg Hkh ugha ikrk"). Their interaction — the lamp's futile resistance against the night's persistence — structures the poem's dialectic of intellectual awakening versus systemic entrapment. A student who analyzes them in isolation misses the dynamic tension that generates the poem's tragic energy.

questions.q: Evaluate this claim: "Muktibodh's use of irony in 'vkReifjp;' undermines the poem's revolutionary potential by making the speaker too self-deprecating." Defend or refute with textual evidence.
questions.a: Refute. The irony does not undermine but *enables* revolutionary potential: by exposing the gap between revolutionary rhetoric ("I am the enemy of darkness") and lived compromise ("I never gave the message of fire"), Muktibodh performs the very self-critique necessary for authentic political consciousness. The closing lines — "My relation with darkness is of love-hate... my life is the companion of contradictions" — transform self-deprecation into dialectical honesty. A student agreeing with the claim confesses a preference for heroic simplicity over Muktibodh's demanding ethical complexity.

questions.q: Write a 4-line stanza using ONE symbol from "vkReifjp;" (lamp, road, night, mirror) and ONE type of irony (verbal/situational) to express a contemporary student's struggle with academic pressure.
questions.a: Example: "I carry a lamp called 'future' / but its oil is borrowed from sleep / the road promises 'success' / yet every milestone mocks my pace." (Symbol: lamp/road; Irony: situational — the tools of progress become instruments of depletion.) A poor answer uses the symbol decoratively without irony or vice versa, showing failure to integrate device and meaning — the core skill for creative application in competitive exams like CUET.
